hook: I'm not married, but **I want to be a parent.**
hook_q: Can I adopt as a single parent?

slides.title: **Yes**, singles can adopt.
slides.body: A single or divorced person can also adopt, subject to meeting the **eligibility criteria.** You apply through CARA, a statutory body of the Women and Child Development Ministry.

slides.title: But **gender** matters.
slides.body: Through CARA, a single woman can adopt a child of **any gender.** A single man cannot adopt a girl child.
slides.ref: Juvenile Justice Act 2015 · Sec 57(4); Adoption Regulations 2022 · Reg 5(2)(c)

slides.title: You must be **ready.**
slides.body: You should be physically fit, financially sound, mentally alert and highly motivated to adopt a child, and physically, mentally and emotionally stable.
slides.ref: Juvenile Justice Act 2015 · Sec 57; Adoption Regulations 2022 · Reg 5(1)

slides.title: Age limits **for singles.**
list: Child up to 2 years: you can be up to 40
Child above 2, up to 4: up to 45
Child above 4, up to 8: up to 50
Child above 8, up to 18: up to 55

slides.title: The **steps.**
list: Register on **CARINGS**; upload documents within 30 days.
An agency or DCPU does your **Home Study Report.**
Reserve a referred child within **48 hours.**
The DM issues the adoption order within **60 days** of application.
slides.ref: Adoption Regulations 2022; CARA / NIPCCD Handbook for DMs

slides.title: Order by the **DM**, not a court.
slides.body: After the 2021 amendment, District Magistrates, including Additional District Magistrates, issue adoption orders (since 2022). Earlier, this power was exercised by the courts.

sources: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 (as amended in 2021) – Sections 57, 61
Central Adoption Resource Authority, MWCD (cara.wcd.gov.in) – eligibility criteria
NIPCCD Handbook for District Magistrates on adoption; PIB releases (MWCD)
caption:
Single and want to adopt? The law allows it. Here's how. 👇

1️⃣ A single or divorced person can adopt if they meet the eligibility criteria
2️⃣ Through CARA, a single woman can adopt a child of any gender; a single man cannot adopt a girl child
3️⃣ Age limits for singles range from 40 (child up to 2 years) to 55 (child above 8)
4️⃣ There must be at least a 25-year age gap between you and the child
5️⃣ Register on CARINGS, CARA's online portal; a Home Study Report follows
6️⃣ The District Magistrate issues the adoption order

Source: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 (Sec 57, 61); Adoption Regulations, 2022 (Reg 5)
